the great trade collapse had a negligible effect on the extensive margin of trade and a positive effect on the intensive margin, while the export status of firms was a good predictor of their resilience to the crisis and their subsequent performance.

the Spanish export miracle was driven by a strong increase in the export intensities of firms, and that the export intensities increased for all firms, including firms that were already exporting before the crisis.

(i) there was no significant change in the number of exporting firms in the aftermath of financial crisis; (ii) there was a significant increase in export intensity; (iii) exporters were more productive and more resilient to the financial crisis than non-exporting firms; (iv) aggregate productivity declined in many industries; (v) improved competitiveness due to internal devaluation and a strong substitutive relationship between exports and domestic sales might explain the export miracle.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Spanish export miracle was not only driven by a strong increase of export intensity of firms, but also by an increase in the number of firms exporting.
the Spanish export miracle is not a miracle at all, but rather the consequence of a large and persistent increase in export intensity at the firm level.
the Spanish economy has been able to withstand the global recession of 2008/2009 better than many other countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crisis did not lead to an increase in export intensity of Spanish firms, but that the firms that were exporting in 2007 continued to do so in 2011 and that they increased their export intensity.

the financial crisis and the great trade collapse have had a profound effect on the internationalization of Spanish firms, and that exporters were more likely to survive and to grow after the crisis than nonexporters.
the Spanish economy was able to weather the great trade collapse and the global recession better than many observers expected, thanks to the resilience of its exporting sector.
